overview: Carolingian rulers made learning, Christian worship and patronage part of imperial government. Their workshops and scholars adapted older traditions into books, buildings and objects that influenced medieval Europe.

items.text: The drive for accurate, readable texts encouraged Carolingian minuscule, a clear script based on Roman letter forms.
Charlemagne gathered scholars including Alcuin, Theodulf and Paul the Lombard. Court patronage supported educational and liturgical reform.
Illuminated books and carved ivory panels combined classical figures with local ornamental traditions. Precious bindings could include gems and pearls.
The palace chapel at Aachen has an octagonal core, an encircling aisle, upper galleries and a dome. Its antique columns were probably brought from Rome and Ravenna.
Charlemagne received the imperial crown in Rome in 800. The ceremony tied royal authority to a Christian interpretation of Roman imperial tradition.
Carolingian art continued after Charlemagne's death and political fragmentation. The end of a unified realm did not end its workshops or manuscript traditions.
